text.p: These are the leading stories in Zimbabwe's state-owned Herald newspaper on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Zimbabwean government will soon announce a revised tariff regime, the president of the Confederation of Zimbabwe Industries (CZI) Jonee Blanchfield said at the weekend. She gave no specific date when she addressed a Chartered Institute of Secretaries dinner in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe's second largest city, but said government was still consulting the private sector.
President Robert Mugabe's government announced new tarrifs earlier this year but scrapped them just after a week amid complaints they were biased against Zimbabwean manufacturers.
- The Zimbabwean army is considering growing its own food to cut costs currently accounting for 11 percent of Zimbabwe's national budget, Defence Minister Moven Mahachi said.
Mahachi also told the state news agency ZIANA the government would probe the alleged abuse by senior military officers of a Z$30 million Zimbabwe Defence Forces Benefit Fund.

- The South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission is said to be at loggerheads with its country's foreign ministry over apartheid spies recruited from Zimbabwean citizens who are now serving life jail terms in Harare. The Herald quoted reliable sources as saying the ministry had refused a commission request to ask the Zimbabwean government to release the spies because it knew Harare would refuse.
